questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's braking power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How long should a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: You do not need to do it before every ride

questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. A thorough inspection takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or with your turn signals. A left arm extended straight out means you plan to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: How should you apply the front brake?

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure
Grab the brake with only two fingers
Press down on the brake lever with your foot

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure
questions.explanation: To apply the front brake, squeeze the brake lever firmly and smoothly with all four fingers. Apply more force gradually.

questions.question: When should you ride with your headlight on?

options.text: Only if you think it helps

questions.explanation: Always keep your headlight on while riding, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to notice you.

questions.question: What kind of pants should a motorcycle rider wear for protection?

options.text: Loose enough to flap in the wind
Short pants that show some leg

questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy synthetic material that cover your entire legs. They should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but not so tight that they restrict movement.

questions.question: What is a common cause of motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riders with little experience on their motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with little experience on their motorcycle
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders who have little experience on their motorcycle.

questions.question: What happens when your rear tire skids?

options.text: You lose the ability to change direction
It is only dangerous if the front tire is also skidding

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose the ability to change direction
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is very dangerous and can cause a violent crash. Too much rear brake pressure can lock the rear wheel. When the rear wheel locks, you cannot change direction. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing while riding?
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and brightly-colored clothing whenever you ride. Crashes happen in bright daylight and at night, so stay visible at all times.

questions.question: How do convex mirrors affect how you see other cars?
questions.explanation: Curved, or convex, mirrors give you a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, objects appear farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: When riding at night, which action should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam light, if possible.

questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance to avoid crashes. Use headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Use your high beam light, except when following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: Which item gives a motorcyclist the best protection?

options.text: A jacket that allows the arms to be exposed.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. Boots or shoes should be tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Use low heels that won't catch on foot pegs. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: How can you help a driver on an entrance ramp merge safely?

options.text: Stay in your lane. It is not your responsibility to be seen.
Change to a lane away from the entrance ramp, if possible.
Weave within your lane to be more obvious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a lane away from the entrance ramp, if possible.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space to enter traffic safely. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if you can do so safely. If there is no other lane, adjust your speed to make space for the merging driver.

questions.question: How is the motorcycle accelerator controlled?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip and is controlled with your right hand.

questions.question: What should you do when going through a turn on a motorcycle?

options.text: Keep your eyes focused close to the front of the motorcycle.
Look through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Increase your speed before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When should reflective clothing be worn?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials all the time to stay visible.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, what should the motorcyclist tell them to do?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Mount the motorcycle after the engine has started.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mount the motorcycle after the engine has started.
questions.explanation: Give your passenger complete safety instructions before you leave. Ask them to get on only after you have started the engine. They should sit as close to you as possible without crowding you and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt firmly. They should keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What is a major effect of drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down physical and mental functions in your body.

questions.question: What should you see when you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane beside you. You may see the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Slow down, approach the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, approach the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If a dog chases you, slow down and approach it. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have a manual transmission. Downshifting to a lower gear slows you down.

questions.question: When you approach an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat so:

options.text: You can jump off if needed.
Your legs can absorb the shock.
Other drivers can see you better.
You can see the surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the impact. This prevents the bump from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a flat tire. You are more likely to notice a sudden change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good replacement for a face shield or goggles.
